intro: The Major Depressive Episode is a psychosocial scoring tool used in paediatric practice. DSM-5 criteria - symptoms in the same 2-week period, a change from previous function. It scores 9 criteria and interprets the total across 2 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in psychosocial
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 9 criteria: Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day (children/adolescents: can be irritable mood); Markedly diminished interest or pleasure in almost all activities; Significant weight change or appetite change (children: failure to make expected weight gain); Insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day; Psychomotor agitation or retardation observable by others; Fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day; Feelings of worthlessness or excessive/inappropriate guilt; Diminished ability to think or concentrate; indecisiveness; Recurrent thoughts of death, suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt/plan. Totals are then banded: any score - Below threshold: fewer than 5 symptoms in the same 2-week period; 5 criteria met or more - Threshold met: ≥5 symptoms over the same 2 weeks - and at least ONE must be depressed mood or loss of interest. Assess suicide risk now and arrange mental-health review.
guidelineRefs: DSM-5 threshold: 5 or more of the 9 criteria listed.
A diagnosis also requires clinically significant distress or impairment, the required duration, and exclusion of substance use or another condition. Screening aid only - not a diagnosis.
At least one of the first two criteria (depressed mood / anhedonia) must be present.
Always ask directly about suicidal ideation and safety, regardless of total.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Major Depressive Episode use?
faqs.a: 9. They are Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day (children/adolescents: can be irritable mood); Markedly diminished interest or pleasure in almost all activities; Significant weight change or appetite change (children: failure to make expected weight gain); Insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day; Psychomotor agitation or retardation observable by others; Fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day; and others.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the Major Depressive Episode mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: any score - Below threshold: fewer than 5 symptoms in the same 2-week period; 5 criteria met or more - Threshold met: ≥5 symptoms over the same 2 weeks - and at least ONE must be depressed mood or loss of interest. Assess suicide risk now and arrange mental-health review.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?
faqs.a: DSM-5 threshold: 5 or more of the 9 criteria listed.
Yes. Score definitions are bundled with the PediAid app, so the score computes without a connection.
